While the squash roasts, wash and dry the remaining fresh produce.
Cut out and discard the stems, ribs, and seeds of the peppers; medium dice.
Cut off and discard the root ends of the scallions; thinly slice, separating the white bottoms and green tops.
Quarter the lime.
Grate the Monterey Jack cheese on the large side of a box grater.

While the squash continues to roast, pat the chicken dry with paper towels; season with salt and pepper. In a large pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the seasoned chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, 6 to 8 minutes, or until browned and cooked through.
Leaving any browned bits (or fond) in the pan, transfer the cooked chicken to a large bowl and set aside in a warm place.

To the pan of reserved fond, add the peppers; season with salt and pepper. (If the pan seems dry, add 1 teaspoon of olive oil.) Cook on medium-high, stirring occasionally, 2 to 3 minutes, or until slightly softened. Add the white bottoms of the scallions; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes, or until slightly softened. Add all but a pinch of the spice blend. Cook, stirring frequently, 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until fragrant. Add 1/2 cup of water and cook, stirring occasionally, 2 to 3 minutes, or until thickened and saucy.
Transfer to the bowl of cooked chicken; add the juice of 1 lime wedge. Stir to combine and season with salt and pepper to taste.

While the sauce cooks, place the tortillas on a sheet pan. Drizzle with olive oil; turn to coat. Arrange in a single layer and toast in the oven 5 to 6 minutes, or until golden brown and slightly crispy. Leaving the oven on, remove the toasted tortillas from the oven and carefully top with the Monterey Jack cheese. Return to the oven and bake 2 to 3 minutes, or until the tortillas are lightly browned and the cheese has melted. Remove from the oven; carefully divide between 2 dishes.

Top the toasted tortillas with the finished chicken. Garnish with half the Cotija cheese, the sour cream, and the green tops of the scallions. Top the roasted squash with the juice of 1 lime wedge, the remaining spice blend and the remaining Cotija cheese. Transfer to a serving dish.
Serve the tostadas and squash with the remaining lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
notes: Prep time: 15 minutes. Cook time: 35-45 minutes. Wine pairing: Jon E Vino St. Laurent, 2015. Depending on what's best at the farms near you, you may receive a yellow squash, green zucchini, or grey zucchini.

title: Persian-Style Chicken & Crispy Rice with Summer Squash, Currants, & Lemon Yogurt
steps: Preheat the oven to 475°F.

In a small pot, combine the rice, a big pinch of salt, and 1 cup of water. Heat to boiling on high. Once boiling, cover and reduce the heat to low. Cook 12 to 14 minutes, or until the water has been absorbed and the rice is tender. Turn off the heat and fluff the cooked rice with a fork.
Transfer half the cooked rice to a sheet pan; spread into an even layer. Set the remaining cooked rice aside in a warm place.
While the rice cooks, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and thinly slice the onion.
Quarter the squash lengthwise; cut crosswise into 1/4-inch-thick pieces.
Roughly chop the almonds.
Roughly chop the parsley leaves and stems.
Using a peeler, remove the yellow rind of the lemon, avoiding the white pith; mince the rind to get 2 teaspoons of zest (or use a zester). Quarter and deseed the lemon.
Place the currants in a bowl; top with the juice of 2 lemon wedges.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and transfer to a bowl. Season with salt, pepper, and the spice blend; toss to coat.

In a medium pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the seasoned chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, 5 to 7 minutes, or until browned and cooked through. Leaving any browned bits (or fond) in the pan, transfer to a plate and set aside in a warm place.

Add the butter to the pan of reserved fond and heat on medium-high until melted. Add the onion; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 5 to 7 minutes, or until lightly browned and slightly softened. Add the squash; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 5 to 7 minutes, or until softened. Add the almonds, cooked chicken, and half the parsley; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until thoroughly combined. Turn off the heat and season with salt and pepper to taste.
While the vegetables cook, drizzle the sheet pan of cooked rice with olive oil. Bake, stirring halfway through, 7 to 9 minutes, or until lightly browned and crispy.
Remove from the oven and let stand for at least 2 minutes. Carefully transfer to the pot of remaining cooked rice. Stir in the currants (including any liquid). Season with salt and pepper to taste.
While the rice bakes, in a bowl, whisk together the lemon zest, yogurt, the juice of the remaining lemon wedges, and 1 teaspoon of water. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Divide the finished rice between 2 dishes and top with the finished chicken and vegetables. Top with spoonfuls of the lemon yogurt. Garnish with the remaining parsley. Serve with the remaining lemon yogurt on the side. Enjoy!
notes: Prep time: 15 minutes. Cook time: 35-45 minutes. Wine pairing: Crisp & Minerally.

title: Chorizo-Spiced Pork Burgers with Kale & Date Salad
steps: Place an oven rack in the center of the oven, then preheat to 450°F.
Peel the onion and cut crosswise into 1/2-inch-thick rounds, keeping the layers intact.
Place on a sheet pan. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; carefully turn to coat.
Roast, flipping halfway through, 19 to 21 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a fork. Remove from the oven and set aside in a warm place.
While the onion roasts, wash and dry the kale. Remove and discard the stems; thinly slice the leaves.
Pit and roughly chop the dates.
Peel and finely chop the garlic.
Finely chop the peppers.
Halve the buns.
While the onion continues to roast, in a medium bowl, combine the kale, dates, and 3/4 of the vinegar. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to combine.
Set aside to marinate, stirring occasionally, for at least 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

While the kale marinates, in a large bowl, combine the ground pork (removing and discarding the paper lining from the bottom), spice blend, and garlic; season with salt and pepper. Gently mix to combine. Using your hands, form the mixture into two 1/2-inch-thick patties; transfer to a plate.

In a large pan, heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the patties and cook, loosely covering the pan with foil, 3 to 4 minutes per side, or until browned and cooked through. Leaving any browned bits (or fond) in the pan, transfer to a plate.
While the patties cook, in a bowl, combine the peppers, sour cream, remaining vinegar, and a drizzle of olive oil; season with salt and pepper to taste.

Add the buns, cut side down, to the pan of reserved fond. (If the pan seems dry, add 1 teaspoon of olive oil.) Toast on medium-high 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until lightly browned. Transfer to a work surface.
Divide the piquillo sauce among the cut sides of the toasted buns. Top the bun bottoms with the cooked patties and roasted onion (separating into rings before adding). Complete with the bun tops.
Divide the burgers and salad between 2 dishes. Garnish the salad with the cheese. Enjoy!
notes: Time: 25-35 minutes. Wine pairing: Bold & Spicy. Chefs, you may receive green curly, dark green lacinato, or red kale.

title: Cumin-Spiced Roast Pork with Vegetable Fried Rice
steps: Place an oven rack in the center of the oven, then preheat to 450°F. Line a sheet pan with foil.
Pat the pork dry with paper towels. Place in a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Add half the cumin-sichuan sauce; turn to coat. Transfer to the sheet pan.

Roast, carefully flipping the pork halfway through, 25 to 27 minutes, or until cooked through (an instant-read thermometer should register 145°F). Transfer to a cutting board and let rest at least 5 minutes.
While the pork roasts, in a medium pot, combine the rice, a big pinch of salt, and 1 cup of water. Heat to boiling on high.

Once boiling, reduce the heat to low. Cover and cook, without stirring, 12 to 14 minutes, or until the water has been absorbed and the rice is tender. Turn off the heat and fluff with a fork. Cover to keep warm.

While the rice cooks, wash and dry the fresh produce. Peel the carrots; thinly slice into rounds. Peel and roughly chop 2 cloves of garlic. Cut off and discard the root end of the bok choy; roughly chop. Crack the egg into a bowl; season with salt and pepper and beat until smooth.
In a separate bowl, combine the mayonnaise and remaining cumin-sichuan sauce.
While the pork continues to roast, in a large pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat a drizzle of olive oil on medium-high until hot.
Add the sliced carrots; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 3 to 4 minutes, or until lightly browned and slightly softened.

Add the chopped garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until slightly softened. Add the chopped bok choy; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 1 to 2 minutes, or until softened.

Using a spoon, move the vegetables to one side of the pan. Add a drizzle of olive oil to the other side, then add the beaten egg. Cook, constantly stirring the egg, 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until cooked through. Stir the vegetables and egg to thoroughly combine.
Transfer to a large bowl. Taste, then season with salt and pepper if desired. Wipe out the pan.
While the pork rests, in the same pan, heat the ghee on medium-high until melted.
Add the cooked rice in an even layer. Cook, without stirring, 3 to 4 minutes, or until slightly crispy.
Turn off the heat and stir in the soy sauce. Transfer to the bowl of cooked vegetables and egg; stir to combine. Taste, then season with salt and pepper if desired.
Find the lines of muscle (or grain) on the rested pork; thinly slice crosswise against the grain.
Serve the sliced pork and fried rice with the cumin mayo. Enjoy!
notes: Time: 30-40 minutes. Wine pairing: Light & Bright.

title: Fresh Fettuccine & Prosciutto with Kale & Tomato Sauce
steps: Heat a medium pot of salted water to boiling on high.
Remove and discard the paper linings between the slices of prosciutto. Stack the prosciutto and thinly slice crosswise.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and roughly chop the garlic. Peel and thinly slice the shallot.
Remove and discard the kale stems; roughly chop the leaves.
Place the tomatoes in a bowl; gently break apart with your hands.
Grate the Grana Padano cheese on the small side of a box grater.
In a large pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil on medium-high until hot.
Add the sliced prosciutto and cook, stirring frequently and breaking apart any clumps, 1 to 2 minutes, or until lightly browned and fragrant.
Leaving any browned bits (or fond) in the pan, transfer to a paper towel-lined plate.

Add the chopped garlic and sliced shallot to the pan of reserved fond. (If the pan seems dry, add a drizzle of olive oil.) Cook on medium-high, stirring frequently, 1 to 2 minutes, or until softened and fragrant.

Add the chopped kale and as much of the red pepper flakes as you'd like, depending on how spicy you'd like the dish to be. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes, or until the kale is slightly wilted.
Add the tomatoes and 1/2 cup of water. Cook, stirring occasionally, 5 to 7 minutes, or until the kale has wilted and the sauce has thickened.
While the sauce cooks, using your hands, carefully separate the strands of the pasta. Add to the pot of boiling water and cook 2 to 3 minutes, or until al dente (still slightly firm to the bite).
Reserving 1/2 cup of the pasta cooking water, drain thoroughly.

Add the cooked pasta, browned prosciutto, and half the reserved pasta cooking water to the pan. Cook, stirring vigorously, 1 to 2 minutes, or until thoroughly coated. (If the sauce seems dry, gradually add the remaining pasta cooking water to achieve your desired consistency.) Turn off the heat.
Stir in the mascarpone cheese; season with pepper to taste.
Garnish the finished pasta with the grated Grana Padano cheese. Enjoy!
notes: Time: 25-35 minutes. Wine pairing: Light & Fresh. Hold off on seasoning with salt until after you've tasted the finished dish! Chefs, you may receive green curly, dark green lacinato, or red kale.

title: Pork Cacciatore with Tomatoes & Fregola Sarda Pasta
steps: Heat a small pot of salted water to boiling on high.
Wash and dry the oregano. Pick the oregano leaves off the stems; discard the stems.
Once the pot of water is boiling, add the pasta and cook 14 to 16 minutes, or until al dente (still slightly firm to the bite). Turn off the heat. Drain thoroughly and return to the pot.
Add the capers, half the oregano, and a drizzle of olive oil. Stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Set aside in a warm place.
While the pasta cooks, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
In a medium pan, heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot.
Add the seasoned pork chops and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side, or until browned and cooked through.
Leaving any browned bits (or fond) in the pan, transfer to a plate. Set aside in a warm place to rest for at least 5 minutes.
While the pork chops cook, wash and dry the pepper and tomatoes.
Cut off and discard the pepper stem. Halve the pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the ribs and seeds. Thinly slice lengthwise.
Halve the tomatoes. Place in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.

Add the pepper to the pan of reserved fond; season with salt and pepper. (If the pan seems dry, add 2 teaspoons of olive oil.) Cook on medium-high, stirring occasionally, 2 to 3 minutes, or until lightly browned and slightly softened.
Add the tomato paste. Cook, stirring frequently, 1 to 2 minutes, or until dark red and fragrant.

To the pan, add the seasoned tomatoes and as much of the red pepper flakes as you'd like, depending on how spicy you'd like the dish to be. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes, or until the tomatoes have softened.

Add the vinegar and 1/2 cup of water (be careful, as the liquid may splatter); season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently and scraping up any fond from the bottom of the pan, 2 to 3 minutes, or until slightly thickened and saucy. Turn off the heat. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Divide the finished pasta and rested pork chops between 2 dishes. Top with the finished vegetables. Garnish with the remaining oregano. Enjoy!
notes: Time: 25-35 minutes. Wine pairing: Plush & Fruity. Chefs, your tomatoes may be red or yellow, and your pepper may be green, purple, or streaked with red!

title: Pork Burgers & Blistered Shishito Peppers with Cucumber & Heritage Globe Tomato Salad
steps: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut off and discard the pepper stems. Place the peppers in a bowl and drizzle with olive oil; toss to coat.
Quarter the tomatoes; place in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Halve the buns.
Peel and finely chop the garlic; using the flat side of your knife, smash until it resembles a paste (or use a zester).
Quarter the cucumber lengthwise. Grate 1 of the quarters on the large side of a box grater. Medium dice the remaining cucumber.
In a bowl, combine the grated cucumber, sour cream, as much of the garlic paste as you'd like, and a drizzle of olive oil; season with salt and pepper to taste.
Blister the peppers: Heat a medium, dry pan (or dry cast iron pan, if you have one) on high until hot.

Add the peppers (including any oil from the bowl) in a single layer. Cook, without stirring, 3 to 4 minutes, or until browned and blistered. Season with salt and pepper. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, 2 to 3 minutes, or until browned and softened.
Transfer to a cutting board. When cool enough to handle, roughly chop. Wipe out the pan.
Make the salad: While the peppers blister, pick the mint leaves off the stems; discard the stems.

In a large bowl, combine the seasoned tomatoes, diced cucumber, half the mint (tearing the leaves just before adding), and a drizzle of olive oil. Stir to thoroughly combine; season with salt and pepper to taste.
Form & cook the patties: In a large bowl, combine the ground pork (removing and discarding the paper lining from the bottom) and spice blend; season with salt and pepper. Gently mix to combine.
Using your hands, form the mixture into two 1/2-inch-thick patties; transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the patties; cook, loosely covering the pan with foil, 3 to 4 minutes per side, or until browned and cooked through.
Leaving any browned bits (or fond) in the pan, transfer to a plate.

Toast the buns: Add the buns, cut side down, to the pan of reserved fond. (If the pan seems dry, add 1 teaspoon of olive oil.) Toast on medium-high 1 to 2 minutes, or until lightly browned. Transfer to a work surface.
Finish & plate your dish: Evenly divide the sauce among the cut sides of the toasted buns. Top the bun bottoms with the cooked patties and chopped peppers. Complete the burgers with the bun tops.
Divide the burgers and salad between 2 dishes. Garnish the salad with the remaining mint (tearing the leaves just before adding). Enjoy!
notes: TIME: 35-45 minutes. Wine pairing: Plush & Fruity. Chefs, shishito peppers are mild, but about one in ten can have quite a kick!

title: Roasted Pork & Mustard Pan Sauce with Asparagus & Fingerling Potatoes
steps: Sear & roast the pork: Remove the pork from the refrigerator to bring to room temperature. Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line a sheet pan with aluminum foil. Pat the pork dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper on all sides.

In a large, high-sided pan (or pot), heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the seasoned pork and cook, turning occasionally, 6 to 8 minutes, or until browned on all sides. Turn off the heat. Leaving any browned bits (or fond) in the pan on the stove, transfer to the prepared sheet pan.

Roast 14 to 16 minutes, or until the pork is cooked through. (An instant-read thermometer should register 145°F.) Remove from the oven. Leaving any juices on the sheet pan, transfer the roasted pork to a cutting board and let rest for at least 5 minutes.
Prepare the ingredients: While the pork sears, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch-thick rounds.
Peel and thinly slice the shallot.
Cut off and discard the tough, woody stem ends of the asparagus; cut into 1-inch pieces on an angle, leaving the pointed tips intact.
Quarter and deseed the lemon.
Pick the tarragon leaves off the stems; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves.
Cook the potatoes: While the pork roasts, in a large pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot.
Add the potatoes and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 6 to 8 minutes, or until browned and softened.
Add the shallot & asparagus: Add the shallot and asparagus to the pan; season with salt and pepper. (If the pan seems dry, add a drizzle of olive oil.)
Cook, stirring occasionally, 3 to 5 minutes, or until the asparagus is bright green and tender. Turn off the heat; season with salt and pepper to taste.
Make the pan sauce: While the vegetables cook, heat the pan of reserved fond on medium-high until hot.
Add the butter, mustard, the juice of all 4 lemon wedges, 2 tablespoons of water, and any juices from the sheet pan.
Cook, stirring constantly and scraping up any fond from the bottom of the pan, 1 to 2 minutes, or until thoroughly combined.
Turn off the heat and stir in the tarragon. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice the pork & plate your dish: Find the lines of muscle (or grain) on the rested pork; thinly slice crosswise against the grain.
Divide the cooked vegetables and sliced pork between 2 dishes. Top the pork with the pan sauce. Enjoy!
notes: PREP TIME: 15 minutes. COOK TIME: 30-40 minutes. Wine pairing: Mt. Beautiful Pinot Gris, 2016.

title: Shrimp & Spaghetti Marinara with Spinach
steps: Prepare the ingredients: Heat a large pot of salted water to boiling on high.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and roughly chop the garlic.
Place the tomatoes in a bowl; gently break apart with your hands.
Roughly chop the parsley leaves and stems.
Cook the spaghetti: Add the spaghetti to the pot of boiling water. Cook 7 to 9 minutes, or until just shy of al dente (still slightly firm to the bite).
Turn off the heat. Reserving 1/2 cup of the spaghetti cooking water, drain thoroughly and return to the pot.
Make the sauce: While the spaghetti cooks, in a large pan, heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot.
Add the garlic; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 1 to 2 minutes, or until slightly softened and fragrant.

Add the tomatoes (be careful, as the liquid may splatter) and as much of the red pepper flakes as you'd like, depending on how spicy you'd like the dish to be; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes, or until slightly thickened and saucy.
Cook the shrimp: While the pasta continues to cook, pat the shrimp dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the seasoned shrimp to the pan of sauce and cook, stirring occasionally, 2 to 3 minutes, or until the shrimp are opaque and cooked through. Turn off the heat.

Finish the spaghetti: To the pot of cooked spaghetti, add the cooked shrimp and sauce, spinach, butter, verjus, and half the reserved spaghetti cooking water; season with salt and pepper. Cook on medium-high, stirring vigorously, 1 to 2 minutes, or until the spaghetti is coated and the spinach has wilted. (If the sauce seems dry, gradually add the remaining spaghetti cooking water to achieve your desired consistency.)
Turn off the heat and stir in half the parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Plate your dish: Divide the finished spaghetti between 2 dishes. Garnish with the remaining parsley. Enjoy!
notes: TIME: 15-25 minutes. Wine pairing: Light & Fresh.

title: Crispy Buttermilk Catfish with Roasted Delicata Squash
steps: Prepare & roast the squash: Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the squash; cut off and discard the ends. Halve lengthwise; using a spoon, scoop out and discard the pulp and seeds. Cut crosswise into 1/4-inch-thick pieces.
Place on a sheet pan. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to thoroughly coat. Arrange in an even layer.
Roast 20 to 22 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a fork. Remove from the oven.
Prepare the remaining ingredients & make the sauce: While the squash roasts, wash and dry the remaining fresh produce.
Cut off and discard the root ends of the scallions; thinly slice, separating the white bottoms and green tops.
Remove and discard the kale stems; roughly chop the leaves.
In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise, pickle relish, and half the vinegar. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Cook the kale: While the squash continues to roast, in a medium pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the white bottoms of the scallions; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes, or until slightly softened.

Add the kale; cook, stirring frequently, 1 to 2 minutes, or until slightly wilted. Add 1/4 cup of water and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 3 to 4 minutes, or until the kale has wilted and the water has cooked off.
Turn off the heat; stir in the remaining vinegar. Transfer to a bowl. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Set aside in a warm place. Wipe out the pan.
Coat the catfish: While the kale cooks, place the spice blend on a plate.
Place the buttermilk in a medium bowl; season with salt and pepper.
Pat the catfish fillets dry with paper towels; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Working 1 piece at a time, thoroughly coat the seasoned fillets in the spice blend (tapping off any excess), then in the buttermilk (letting any excess drip off), then again in the spice blend (pressing to adhere). Transfer to a separate plate.
Cook the catfish: While the squash continues to roast, in the same pan, heat a thin layer of oil on medium-high until hot.

Once the oil is hot enough that a pinch of the spice blend sizzles immediately when added to the pan, add the coated catfish fillets. Cook 3 to 5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate; immediately season with salt and pepper.
Plate your dish: Divide the cooked catfish fillets, cooked kale, and roasted squash between 2 dishes. Serve with the sauce on the side. Garnish with the green tops of the scallions. Enjoy!
notes: TIME: 35-45 minutes. Wine pairing: Zesty & Tropical. Chefs, depending on what's freshest at the farms near you, your kale may be dark green lacinato, green curly, or red.

title: Herb-Crusted Rockfish & Butter Pan Sauce with Garlic-Sautéed Kale & Mashed Potatoes
steps: Cook & mash the potatoes: Heat a small pot of salted water to boiling on high.
Wash, dry, and medium dice the potatoes.

Once the pot of water is boiling, add the potatoes and cook 9 to 11 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a fork. Turn off the heat. Drain thoroughly and return to the pot. Add 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
Using a fork, mash to your desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Set aside in a warm place.
Prepare the remaining ingredients: While the potatoes cook, wash and dry the remaining fresh produce.
Remove and discard the kale stems; roughly chop the leaves.
Peel and roughly chop the garlic.
Pick the thyme leaves off the stems; discard the stems.
Quarter and deseed the lemon.

Cook the kale: While the potatoes continue to cook, in a large pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the kale, half the garlic, and as much of the red pepper flakes as you'd like, depending on how spicy you'd like the dish to be. Season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 1 to 2 minutes, or until fragrant and the kale is slightly wilted.

Add 1/4 cup of water; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 3 to 4 minutes, or until the kale has wilted and the water has cooked off. Turn off the heat. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Transfer to a plate and set aside in a warm place. Wipe out the pan.

Bread the rockfish: Crack the egg into a medium bowl and beat until smooth. Place the flour on a large plate; season with salt and pepper. Place the breadcrumbs and thyme on a separate large plate; season with salt and pepper and stir to combine.

Pat the rockfish fillets dry with paper towels; season with salt and pepper on both sides. Working 1 at a time, thoroughly coat the seasoned fillets in the flour (tapping off any excess), then in the beaten egg (letting any excess drip off), then in the breadcrumbs (pressing to adhere). Transfer to a separate plate.

Cook the rockfish: In the same pan, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the breaded rockfish fillets and cook 2 to 3 minutes per side, or until browned and cooked through. Leaving any browned bits (or fond) in the pan, transfer to a paper towel-lined plate; immediately season with salt and pepper.

Make the pan sauce & plate your dish: Add the butter, remaining garlic, the juice of all 4 lemon wedges, and 2 tablespoons of water to the pan of reserved fond. Cook on medium-high, stirring constantly and scraping up any fond, 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until thoroughly combined and the butter has melted. Turn off the heat. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Divide the mashed potatoes, cooked kale, and cooked rockfish fillets between 2 dishes. Top the potatoes and rockfish with the pan sauce. Enjoy!
notes: TIME: 25-35 minutes. Wine pairing: Crisp & Minerally. Inspired by a gourmet dish from the August 30 episode of MasterChef Season 8 on FOX.

title: Salmon & Udon Noodle Stir-Fry with Sweet Peppers, Bok Choy, & Furikake
steps: Prepare the ingredients: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut off and discard the pepper stems. Halve the peppers lengthwise; remove and discard the ribs and seeds. Thinly slice crosswise.
Peel and finely chop the garlic.
Peel and finely chop the ginger.
Cut off and discard the root ends of the scallions; thinly slice on an angle, separating the white bottoms and green tops.
Cut off and discard the root ends of the bok choy; roughly chop.
Cook the salmon: Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
In a medium pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil on medium-high until hot.
Add the seasoned fillets, skinless side down. Cook 3 to 4 minutes on the first side, or until lightly browned.
Flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes, or until lightly browned and cooked to your desired degree of doneness. Turn off the heat.
Start the stir-fry: While the salmon cooks, in a large pan, heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot.
Add the peppers and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 2 to 3 minutes, or until softened and fragrant.

Add the aromatics & bok choy: Add the garlic, ginger, white bottoms of the scallions, and bok choy to the pan; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes, or until slightly softened.
Add the vinegar; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until combined.

Finish the stir-fry: Add the noodles (carefully separating with your hands before adding) and 1/3 cup of water to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes, or until the noodles are coated and heated through.
Turn off the heat; stir in the sushi sauce and sesame oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Plate your dish: Divide the finished stir-fry between 2 dishes. Top with the cooked salmon fillets. Garnish with the green tops of the scallions and furikake. Enjoy!
notes: TIME: 25-35 minutes. Wine pairing: Lush & Fruity.

title: Cornmeal-Crusted Shrimp Po' Boys with Tomato & Cucumber Salad
steps: Prepare the ingredients: Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Remove and discard the corn husks and silks. Cut the corn kernels off the cob; discard the cob.
Peel the cucumber, leaving alternating strips of skin intact. Halve lengthwise; using a spoon, scoop out and discard the seeds. Cut the cucumber crosswise into 1/2-inch-thick pieces.
Medium dice the tomatoes. Place in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Cut the chives into 1/2-inch pieces.
Halve the rolls.

Cook the corn & make the rémoulade: In a medium pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 1 teaspoon of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the corn in an even layer. Cook, without stirring, 1 to 2 minutes, or until lightly browned and slightly softened. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes, or until browned. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a medium bowl. Add the pickle relish, creamy mustard sauce, and half the vinegar. Stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Wipe out the pan.

Make the salad: While the corn cooks, in a medium bowl, combine the cucumber, half the seasoned tomatoes, half the chives, the remaining vinegar, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Transfer to a serving dish.
Toast the rolls: Place the rolls on a sheet pan, cut side up. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Toast in the oven 6 to 8 minutes, or until the edges are lightly browned. Remove from the oven. Transfer to a work surface.
Coat & cook the shrimp: While the rolls toast, place the cornmeal in a large bowl.
Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper. Add to the bowl of cornmeal and toss to coat.

In the pan used to cook the corn, heat a thin layer of oil on medium-high until hot. Once the oil is hot enough that a pinch of cornmeal sizzles immediately when added to the pan, add the coated shrimp (tapping off any excess cornmeal before adding) in a single layer. Cook 3 to 4 minutes on the first side, or until lightly browned.
Flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes, or until cooked through. Turn off the heat; season with salt and pepper to taste.

Plate your dish: Divide the rémoulade among the cut sides of the toasted rolls. Top the roll bottoms with the cooked shrimp, remaining seasoned tomatoes, and remaining chives. Complete the sandwiches with the roll tops.
Transfer to a serving dish. Serve the sandwiches with the salad on the side. Enjoy!
notes: TIME: 25-35 minutes. Wine pairing: Crisp & Minerally.

title: Spicy Lemongrass Salmon with Green Beans & Herb Rice
steps: Cook the rice: In a small saucepan, combine the rice, a big pinch of salt, and 1 cup of water. Heat to boiling on high. Once boiling, cover and reduce the heat to low. Cook 12 to 14 minutes, or until the water has been absorbed and the rice is tender. Turn off the heat. Fluff the cooked rice with a fork. Set aside in a warm place.
Prepare the ingredients: While the rice cooks, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut off and discard the stem ends of the green beans.
Cut off and discard the bell pepper stem; halve the bell pepper lengthwise. Remove and discard the ribs and seeds. Thinly slice the bell pepper lengthwise.
Peel and finely chop the ginger.
Cut off and discard the ends of the lemongrass; peel away and discard the fibrous outer layers until you reach the pliable white core. Finely chop the lemongrass core.
Cut off and discard the root ends of the scallions; thinly slice, separating the white bottoms and green tops.
Peel and roughly chop the garlic.
Pick the cilantro and mint leaves off the stems; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves.

Cut off and discard the chile pepper stem. Thinly slice the chile pepper. (For a milder dish, remove and discard the ribs and seeds first.) Thoroughly wash your hands immediately after handling the chile pepper.

Cook the vegetables: In a large pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the green beans, bell pepper, ginger, lemongrass, white bottoms of the scallions, and garlic; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 2 to 3 minutes, or until slightly softened.

Make the sauce & finish the vegetables: To the pan, add the Golden Mountain sauce, vinegar, 1/3 cup of water, and as much of the chile pepper as you'd like, depending on how spicy you'd like the dish to be. Cook, stirring constantly, 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until thoroughly combined and the mixture is slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Transfer to a bowl. Set aside in a warm place. Rinse and wipe out the pan.

Cook the salmon: Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels; season with salt and pepper on both sides. In the same pan, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the seasoned fillets, skinless side down. Cook 3 to 4 minutes on the first side, or until lightly browned. Flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes, or until lightly browned and cooked to your desired degree of doneness. Divide between 2 dishes.
Finish the rice & plate your dish: To the saucepan of cooked rice, stir in half the cilantro and mint.

Divide the finished rice and finished vegetables (reserving the sauce) between the dishes of cooked salmon fillets. Top the salmon with some of the sauce. Garnish with the green tops of the scallions and remaining cilantro and mint. Serve with any remaining sauce. Enjoy!
notes: TIME: 25-35 minutes. Wine pairing: Floral & Aromatic. It may seem intimidating, but it's easy to prep after you peel away the tough outer layers to reveal its fragrant core.

title: Shrimp Rolls with Quick Pickles & Sweet Potato Wedges
steps: Prepare & roast the sweet potatoes: Preheat the oven to 475°F. Wash and dry the sweet potatoes. Cut the sweet potatoes lengthwise into 1/2-inch-wide wedges. Place on a sheet pan. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat. Arrange in a single, even layer.
Roast 24 to 26 minutes, or until browned and tender when pierced with a fork. Remove the roasted sweet potatoes from the oven. Transfer to a serving dish and set aside in a warm place.
Prepare the remaining ingredients: While the sweet potatoes roast, wash and dry the remaining fresh produce.
Peel the garlic; using the flat side of your knife, gently smash each clove to flatten.
Roughly chop half the dill. Keep the remaining dill sprigs whole.
Quarter and deseed the lemon.
Quarter the cucumber lengthwise; halve crosswise. Place in a medium heatproof bowl; top with the juice of 2 lemon wedges. Toss to coat.
If necessary, halve the buns, keeping the bottoms intact.
Thinly slice the celery.

Cut off and discard the stem end of the pepper; halve lengthwise, then remove and discard the ribs and seeds. Thinly slice the pepper crosswise. Thoroughly wash your hands and cutting board immediately after handling the pepper.

Make the pickles: While the sweet potatoes continue to roast, in a small pot, combine the vinegar, sugar, garlic, whole dill sprigs, a big pinch of salt, and 1/4 cup of water; heat to boiling on high. Once boiling, cook, without stirring, 2 to 4 minutes, or until the liquid is slightly reduced in volume.
Carefully pour into the bowl of cucumber; stir to coat. Set aside to cool, stirring occasionally, for at least 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Cook the shrimp: While the pickles cool, rinse the shrimp and pat dry with paper towels; season with salt and pepper. In a medium pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the seasoned shrimp. Cook, stirring occasionally, 2 to 4 minutes, or until opaque and just cooked through. Transfer to a medium bowl.

Toast the buns: While the shrimp cooks, place the buns on a separate sheet pan, cut side up. Toast in the oven 3 to 4 minutes, or until the edges are lightly browned. Remove from the oven and transfer to a work surface.

Dress the shrimp & plate your dish: To the bowl of cooked shrimp, add the celery, creamy mustard sauce, the juice of the remaining lemon wedges, and as much of the pepper as you'd like, depending on how spicy you'd like the dish to be; season with salt and pepper. Stir to thoroughly combine. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Evenly divide the dressed shrimp between the toasted buns.
Divide the shrimp rolls, roasted sweet potatoes, and pickles (discarding the liquid, garlic, and dill sprigs before serving) between 2 dishes. Garnish the rolls with the chopped dill. Enjoy!
notes: PREP TIME: 15 minutes. COOK TIME: 25-35 minutes. Wine pairing: Light & Fresh.

title: Shrimp & Fresh Gnocchi with Corn, Basil, & Cherry Tomatoes
steps: Prepare the ingredients: Heat a large pot of salted water to boiling on high.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut off and discard the root ends of the scallions; thinly slice on an angle.
Remove and discard the corn husks and silks. Cut the corn kernels off the cob; discard the cob.
Peel and roughly chop the garlic.
Pick the basil leaves off the stems; discard the stems.
Blister the tomatoes: In a large pan, heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot.
Add the tomatoes. Cook, without stirring, 3 to 4 minutes, or until browned and blistered. Season with salt and pepper.
Continue to cook, stirring constantly, 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until slightly softened. Transfer to a bowl. Wipe out the pan.
Cook the corn: In the same pan, heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil on medium-high until hot.
Add the scallions and corn; cook, stirring occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes, or until slightly softened. Turn off the heat; season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cook the shrimp: Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper.

To the pan of cooked corn, add the seasoned shrimp, garlic, and as much of the red pepper flakes as you'd like, depending on how spicy you'd like the dish to be. Cook on medium-high, stirring frequently, 3 to 4 minutes, or until the shrimp are opaque and cooked through.
Turn off the heat; season with salt and pepper to taste.

Cook & finish the gnocchi: While the shrimp cook, add the gnocchi to the pot of boiling water. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, or until the gnocchi float to the top of the pot. Reserving 1/3 cup of the gnocchi cooking water, drain thoroughly.

To the pan of cooked shrimp and corn, add the cooked gnocchi, blistered tomatoes, butter, half the reserved gnocchi cooking water, and half the basil (tearing the leaves just before adding). Cook on medium-high, stirring vigorously, 1 to 2 minutes, or until the gnocchi are coated. (If the sauce seems dry, gradually add the remaining gnocchi cooking water to achieve your desired consistency.) Turn off the heat. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Plate your dish: Divide the finished gnocchi between 2 dishes. Garnish with the remaining basil (tearing the leaves just before adding). Enjoy!
notes: PREP TIME: 10 minutes. COOK TIME: 15-25 minutes. Wine pairing: Light & Fresh. Chefs, depending on what's freshest at the farms near you, your tomatoes may be red or yellow.

title: Cod & Tomatillo Salsa with Summer Squash & Sweet Potato Hash
steps: Prepare the ingredients & make the lime sour cream: Preheat the oven to 475°F.
Remove and discard any husks from the tomatillos.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Medium dice the sweet potato.
Medium dice the squash.
Peel and roughly chop the garlic.
Roughly chop the cilantro leaves and stems.
Quarter the lime.
Cut off and discard the root ends of the scallions; thinly slice, separating the white bottoms and green tops.
In a bowl, combine the sour cream, the juice of 2 lime wedges, the green tops of the scallions, 1 tablespoon of water, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Roughly chop the pepper. Thoroughly wash your hands, knife, and cutting board immediately after handling the pepper.

Roast the tomatillos: Line a sheet pan with aluminum foil. Place the tomatillos on the prepared sheet pan. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Turn to thoroughly coat. Roast 12 to 14 minutes, or until lightly browned and softened. Remove from the oven. Carefully transfer to a cutting board.

Make the hash: While the tomatillos roast, in a large pan (nonstick, if you have one), heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the sweet potato in a single, even layer; cook, without stirring, 2 to 3 minutes, or until lightly browned. Season with salt and pepper. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, 2 to 3 minutes, or until browned and slightly softened. Add the squash and cook, stirring occasionally, 2 to 3 minutes, or until lightly browned. Add the garlic and white bottoms of the scallions. Cook, stirring occasionally, 2 to 3 minutes, or until slightly softened and fragrant. Turn off the heat. Stir in the pepitas. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Divide between 2 dishes and set aside in a warm place. Wipe out the pan.

Cook the cod: Pat the cod fillets dry with paper towels; season with salt and pepper on both sides. In the same pan, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the seasoned fillets and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side, or until lightly browned and cooked through. Turn off the heat.

Make the salsa: While the cod cooks, when cool enough to handle, finely chop the roasted tomatillos. Transfer to a medium bowl. Add half the cilantro, the juice of the remaining lime wedges, and as much of the pepper as you'd like, depending on how spicy you'd like the dish to be; season with salt and pepper. Stir to thoroughly combine. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Plate your dish: Top the dishes of hash with the cooked cod fillets. Top the fish with as much of the salsa as you'd like (you may have extra). Garnish with the remaining cilantro. Serve with the lime sour cream on the side. Enjoy!
notes: PREP TIME: 15 minutes. COOK TIME: 25-35 minutes. Wine pairing: Light & Fresh. You may receive green zucchini, grey zucchini, or yellow squash.

title: Tomato-Saffron Risotto with Sautéed Summer Squash & Baby Greens Salad
steps: Prepare the ingredients: wash and dry the fresh produce. Peel and finely chop the shallot. Peel and roughly chop the garlic. Halve the squash lengthwise; cut crosswise into 1/2-inch-thick pieces. Thinly slice the chives.

Start the risotto: in a medium pot, heat 2 tsp olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the shallot and 3/4 of the garlic; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 2-3 minutes, until slightly softened and fragrant. Add the tomato paste and as much red pepper flakes as you'd like; cook, stirring constantly, 1-2 minutes, until dark red and fragrant.

Finish the risotto: add the rice, saffron, and 3 1/2 cups of water to the pot; heat to boiling on high. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-high and cook, stirring occasionally, 14-16 minutes, until most of the liquid is absorbed and the rice is al dente. Turn off the heat. Add the butter and mascarpone cheese; stir to thoroughly combine. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Cook the squash: once the risotto has cooked about 10 minutes, in a medium pan heat 2 tsp olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the squash in a single layer; cook without stirring 3-4 minutes, until browned. Add the remaining garlic; season, and cook, stirring constantly, 30 seconds to 1 minute, until fragrant. Add 1/4 of the vinegar; cook, stirring constantly, 30 seconds to 1 minute, until cooked off. Turn off the heat.
Make the dressing: place the remaining vinegar in a bowl. Slowly whisk in 1 Tbsp olive oil until well combined; season with salt and pepper to taste.

Make the salad and plate your dish: just before serving, combine the baby greens and parmesan cheese in a large bowl. Add enough dressing to coat; gently toss and season to taste. Transfer to a serving dish. Divide the finished risotto between 2 dishes. Top with the cooked squash and chives. Serve with the salad on the side. Enjoy!
notes: Prep time: 10 minutes. Cook time: 20-30 minutes. Blue Apron wine pairing: Fruity & Savory. Chefs note: depending on what's best near you, you may receive grey zucchini, green zucchini, or yellow squash.

title: Asparagus & Summer Squash Curry with Ginger-Lime Peanuts
steps: Prepare the ingredients: wash and dry the fresh produce. Peel and roughly chop the ginger. Roughly chop the peanuts. Using a peeler, remove the green rind of the lime, avoiding the white pith; mince the rind to get 2 tsp of zest. Quarter the lime. Peel and thinly slice the shallot. Peel the carrots and thinly slice into rounds. Medium dice the squash. Cut off and discard the tough, woody stem ends of the asparagus; halve on an angle. Roughly chop the cilantro leaves and stems.

Cook the rice: in a small pot, combine the rice, a big pinch of salt, and 1 cup of water. Heat to boiling on high. Once boiling, cover and reduce heat to low. Cook 12-14 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender. Turn off the heat and fluff the cooked rice with a fork. Set aside in a warm place.

Make the ginger-lime peanuts: while the rice cooks, in a large pan heat 2 tsp olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add half the ginger; cook, stirring constantly, 1-2 minutes, until softened and fragrant. Reduce heat to low; add the peanuts. Cook, stirring frequently, 1-2 minutes, until toasted. Add the lime zest and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, 30 seconds to 1 minute, until fragrant. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and immediately season with salt. Set aside in a warm place. Rinse and wipe out the pan.

Start the curry: while the rice continues to cook, in the same pan heat 2 tsp olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the shallot, carrots, squash, and remaining ginger; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, 3-4 minutes, until slightly softened. Add as much of the curry paste as you'd like, depending on how spicy you'd like the dish to be. Cook, stirring frequently, 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.

Finish the curry: to the pan, add the asparagus, coconut milk (shaking the can just before opening), Golden Mountain sauce, and sugar; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 8-10 minutes, until slightly reduced in volume and the asparagus has softened. Turn off the heat and stir in the juice of 2 lime wedges. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Plate your dish: divide the cooked rice and finished curry between 2 dishes. Garnish with the cilantro and ginger-lime peanuts. Serve with the remaining lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
notes: Prep time: 15 minutes. Cook time: 25-35 minutes. Blue Apron wine pairing: Dancing Crow Sauvignon Blanc, 2016. Chefs note: your squash may be green or grey zucchini, or yellow summer squash.

title: Roasted Onion Miso Ramen with Mustard Greens & Soft-Boiled Eggs
steps: Prepare and roast the onion: preheat the oven to 475°F. Heat a medium pot of salted water to boiling on high. Peel the onion and cut lengthwise into 8 equal-sized wedges. Place the onion on a sheet pan, drizzle with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper; toss to thoroughly coat and arrange in a single, even layer. Roast 18-20 minutes, until browned and tender when pierced with a fork. Remove from the oven.

Prepare the remaining ingredients: while the onion roasts, wash and dry the remaining fresh produce. Quarter the mushrooms. Peel and roughly chop the garlic. Peel and finely chop the ginger. Remove and discard the mustard green stems; thinly slice the leaves. In a medium bowl, whisk together the miso paste and 1/4 cup of warm water.

Cook and peel the eggs: while the onion continues to roast, carefully add the eggs to the pot of boiling water. Cook for exactly 7 minutes. Leaving the water boiling, remove the eggs with a slotted spoon and rinse under cold water for 30 seconds to 1 minute. When cool enough to handle, carefully peel the eggs. Transfer to a cutting board; halve lengthwise.

Start the vegetables: while the eggs cook, in a large, high-sided pan heat 2 tsp olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the mushrooms; cook, stirring occasionally, 3-5 minutes, until lightly browned and slightly softened. Add the garlic and ginger; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, 30 seconds to 1 minute, until fragrant.

Finish the vegetables and make the broth: add the mustard greens to the pan and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1-3 minutes, until slightly wilted. Add the vinegar (careful, it may splatter) and cook, stirring frequently, 1-2 minutes, until cooked off. Add the roasted onion, miso-water mixture, 2 cups of water, and as much sambal oelek as you'd like; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally and separating the layers of onion, 4-6 minutes, until thoroughly combined and the liquid has slightly reduced. Turn off the heat; season with salt and pepper to taste.

Cook the noodles and plate your dish: while the broth cooks, add the noodles to the same pot of boiling water, stirring gently to separate. Cook 2-3 minutes, until tender. Drain thoroughly and rinse under warm water to prevent sticking. Divide the drained noodles between 2 bowls. Top with the kombu, finished vegetables and broth, and halved eggs. Season the eggs with pepper. Enjoy!
notes: Prep time: 15 minutes. Cook time: 35-45 minutes. Blue Apron wine pairing: Jon E Vino St. Laurent, 2015. Note: IMG_6112.jpeg is a duplicate photo of the front card and was excluded.

title: Fresh Mozzarella Pizza & Romaine Salad with Spicy Chile Dressing
steps: Prepare the ingredients: remove the dough from the refrigerator to bring to room temperature. Preheat the oven to 475°F. Wash and dry the fresh produce. Peel and finely chop the garlic; using the flat side of your knife, smash until it resembles a paste (or use a zester). Cut off and discard the root end of the lettuce; thinly slice the leaves. Halve the cucumber lengthwise; thinly slice crosswise.
Make the sauce: in a bowl, combine the tomato sauce, garlic paste, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Assemble and bake the pizza: lightly oil a sheet pan. On a clean, dry work surface, using your hands and a rolling pin (or a wine bottle), gently stretch and roll the dough to a 1/4-inch thickness (if resistant, let rest 5 minutes). Carefully transfer the dough to the prepared sheet pan; rub the dough into the pan to coat the bottom in oil. Leaving a 1-inch border around the edges, evenly top the dough with the sauce and mozzarella cheese (tearing into small pieces before adding). Bake, rotating the sheet pan halfway through, 15-17 minutes, until the cheese has melted and the crust is golden brown. Remove from the oven and let stand for at least 2 minutes.

Make the dressing: while the pizza bakes, in a bowl whisk together the quark cheese, vinegar, and as much of the chile paste as you'd like; season with salt and pepper. Slowly whisk in 2 Tbsp olive oil until well combined. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Make the salad: while the pizza continues to bake, pick the basil leaves off the stems; discard the stems. Just before serving, in a large bowl combine the lettuce, cucumber, and basil (tearing the leaves just before adding); season with salt and pepper. Add enough of the dressing to coat the salad (you may have extra); toss to combine. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Plate your dish: transfer the baked pizza to a cutting board; cut into 6 equal-sized pieces. Top 2/3 of the baked pizza with 2/3 of the salad (you will have extra pizza and salad). Divide the topped pizza between dishes. Enjoy!
notes: Prep time: 10 minutes. Cook time: 30-40 minutes. Blue Apron wine pairing: Fruity & Savory.

title: Broccoli Dip Soup
steps: Cook broccoli in butter as directed.
Add onion, cheese, and mushroom soup, then top with additional cheese.
notes: Handwritten family recipe card. Original instructions are brief/informal - quantities as written on the card.

title: White Stuff
steps: Cut prosciutto/speck into small(ish) pieces.
Thinly slice the green onions, separating the chives from the onion. Roughly mince the garlic, or use a press later when needed.
Heat a skillet on medium heat.
If using pancetta, cook it thoroughly, then remove from the pan.
Bring a pot of water to a boil; once ready, salt the water and cook the pasta.
If not using pancetta, add the butter to the skillet and melt it down.
Add the garlic and onion; let simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Add the heavy cream and half & half. After about a minute, bring the heat down to medium-low to avoid burning or overheating the sauce.
Stir thoroughly.
Add salt, white pepper, onion powder, and garlic powder to taste. For a little kick, add a pinch of red pepper flakes.
Once the sauce is where you like it, add the meat(s) back in along with the chives, then finish with a little parmesan.
If there's enough room in the pan, add the pasta directly and mix together, or pour the sauce over the pasta in a bowl.
Enjoy!
notes: Taught by Dad, who picked it up while traveling in Italy for 2 weeks during the writer's senior year of high school.

title: Tuna Salad
steps: Dice the onion.
Open and drain the cans of tuna.
Mix everything together in a bowl. Use an electric mixer if a whipped texture is preferred.
notes: No servings or attribution specified in original notes.

title: Tomato Chutney
steps: Heat a drizzle of oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and chili flake; cook another minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, vinegar, and salt. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down and the mixture thickens to a jammy consistency, roughly 20-40 minutes depending on desired thickness.
Taste and adjust salt, sugar, or vinegar as needed. Cool before storing.
notes: Recreated from memory - amounts and method are generic placeholders based on typical tomato chutney recipes, not yet verified against the original. Update once tested.

title: Tater Tot Casserole
steps: Brown the ground beef; drain the grease, then let cool for about 5 minutes. Season well with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and Worcestershire sauce while cooking.
Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a casserole dish, mix the beef, cream of mushroom soup, and sour cream together with a large handful of shredded cheddar cheese.
Lay the tater tots over the top.
Bake until the tots are golden brown, then add cheese to the top. Put back in the oven until melted.

title: Cornbread Stuffing
steps: Brown the sausage in a cast iron skillet, keeping it in bigger chunks.
Medium dice the celery and onion.
Cube stale cornbread into 1-inch cubes. If made fresh, pop the cornbread into the oven for a bit to get a "stale" texture.
Saute the onion and celery for 1-2 minutes.
Mix all dry ingredients into a casserole dish; mix together roughly to crumble the cornbread chunks some.
Add chicken stock - you want it soggy, but not submerged.

Cook in the oven at 350-375F for 30-45 minutes. This part is flexible and can go in at a wide range of temps to accommodate other holiday sides cooking at the same time. It is done when everything firms up to the consistency of bread pudding.
notes: Dad's holiday cornbread stuffing recipe.

title: Stuffed Jalapenos
steps: Brown the breakfast sausage in a pan.
Small dice the onion.
Cut the stems off, halve, and deseed the jalapenos.
Remove the sausage from the pan, leaving the grease to saute the onion.
Saute the onion in the pan - can go anywhere from translucent to caramelized based on personal preference.
Drain the grease.

In a large mixing bowl, mix together the sausage, onion, cream cheese, a couple dashes of Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, red chili flake, salt, and fresh cracked pepper. All to taste.
Open the package of bacon and cut the strips in half.
Use a tablespoon to load the filling into the jalapeno halves, or load it into a piping bag and prepare that way.

Once there is a healthy amount of filling on the jalapeno, wrap with bacon. If pulling the bacon straight from the fridge, you might need toothpicks to hold everything together; if you pull the bacon out earlier so it warms slightly, it will be easier to wrap.

title: Sausage Balls

ingredients.name: Italian seasoning (or thyme, rosemary, and sage)
milk
ingredients.unit: to taste (just a dash, easy to overdo)

steps: Preheat oven to 350F.
Mix ingredients together in a mixing bowl.
Add milk if the mixture is too dry - just a dash at a time, as it can go too wet very quickly.
Roll into 3/4 to 1 inch diameter balls.
Lay out onto a baking sheet, making sure they are not touching.
Cook in the oven for 20-25 minutes.

title: Red Salsa
notes: First batch of an original taco hot sauce/salsa, inspired by favorite street tacos over the years (Nicos, OMG, Bachman Taco, Taqueria El Paisano, and others). Steps not yet written - to be added.

title: Green Salsa
notes: First batch of an original taco hot sauce/salsa, inspired by favorite street tacos over the years (Nicos, OMG, Bachman Taco, Taqueria El Paisano, and others). Steps not yet written - to be added. Companion recipe to Red Salsa.

title: Aunt Katie's Salsa
steps: Peel the garlic cloves. Peel and quarter the onion, then separate the quarters into pieces. Remove seeds from the jalapeno.
If tomatillos are large, quarter them. If not, leave whole.

Place the tomatillos, garlic, onion, and jalapeno on foil or parchment paper on a baking sheet. Broil on high for 4-5 minutes until just beginning to blacken. Flip and rotate, then broil another 4-5 minutes.
Let cool until easy to handle. Peel the skin off the tomatillo and jalapeno.
Toss everything into a blender or food processor. Add the cilantro, salt, and lime juice. Pulse until desired consistency is reached.
Taste and adjust salt or lime juice as needed.

title: Mom's Pot Roast

ingredients.name: beef stock
ingredients.unit: to taste (enough to fill crock pot as desired)

steps: Sear the meat.
Put everything into the crock pot and cook all afternoon.
notes: Very loose/informal method as originally written - amounts for most seasonings and liquids were not specified.

title: Pineapple Salsa
steps: Dice all ingredients.
Mix together in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Pimento Cheese
steps: Put everything into a bowl and mix it up.
Eat it.
notes: Inspired by Dad's pimento cheese sandwiches from childhood.

title: Mac n Cheese

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.unit: to taste (added 1 cup at a time)

ingredients.name: cheddar cheese
ingredients.unit: to taste (handfuls, plus extra for topping)

steps: Boil and cook a 1 lb bag of elbow macaroni noodles.
In a pot, melt 6-8 tablespoons of butter (3/4 to 1 stick), or use an equivalent amount of bacon grease.
Sprinkle in about 2 to 2 1/2 tablespoons of flour and mix together until it thickens to the consistency of wet sand.
Slowly add milk, 1 cup at a time, stirring and bringing up the temperature each time.
Add in the cream cheese; continue to stir until fully melted.
Add cheddar cheese a handful at a time, stirring in until fully melted. The sauce should be getting thick again, almost like a runny queso.
Season with the remaining dry ingredients.
Turn off the heat.
In a disposable pan or casserole dish, mix the sauce together with the prepared noodles.
Top with remaining cheddar cheese and breadcrumbs, goldfish, cheez-its, or whatever topping you like.
Bake in the oven at 350-375F for about 45 minutes, or until the top is golden brown.

title: Lime Crema Sauce
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the crema, heavy cream, lime juice, sugar, and salt until smooth.
If a thinner, more drizzle-able consistency is desired, whisk in a little more heavy cream a splash at a time.
Taste and adjust lime juice, sugar, or salt as needed.
notes: Own original recipe, still in development. Amounts/ratios are generic placeholders based on typical lime crema recipes, not yet tested against the intended version - update once dialed in.

title: Lasagna Soup
steps: Brown the Italian/pork sausage in a large pot or Dutch oven; dice the onion while the sausage browns.
Remove the sausage from the pan; add a bit of olive oil and toss in the onions.
Once the onions are translucent, add the tomato paste and let it caramelize a bit, about 1 minute.
Add the garlic and stir in for 30-45 seconds.
Add the peeled tomatoes, cutting or shredding them with your hands.
Add the parsley, oregano, Italian seasoning, red chili flakes, salt, and pepper to taste.
Add the chicken stock.
Add the heavy cream.
Add the sausage back in.
Bring to a boil and add the pasta.
While the pasta cooks, mix the ricotta, mozzarella, and parmesan together in a bowl.
Once the pasta is ready, serve into a bowl, add a dollop of the cheese mixture on top, and top with basil if feeling fancy.
notes: Found by Paige on Instagram; this is the writer's own spin on the original. Pasta amount not yet measured - to be added next time it's made.

title: Hush Puppies
steps: Mix the dry ingredients into a bowl and stir together with a wire whisk.
(If subbing for buttermilk) In a separate bowl, mix the milk and vinegar together. Let sit for 5 minutes.
Mix the wet ingredients together until thoroughly combined.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and fold together until incorporated.
Heat about 2-3 inches of frying oil in a heavy pot or deep fryer to 350F.
Drop rounded spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil, frying in batches to avoid crowding the pot.
Fry for 2-3 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown on all sides.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve warm.
notes: Recipe tweaked together with Dad while staying with him and Cheryl in late 2021. Frying instructions added as a standard method - not yet part of the original notes.

title: Guacamole
steps: Dice the onion, tomato, jalapeno, and cilantro.
Halve and pit the avocados; scoop the flesh into a bowl and mash to desired consistency.
Fold in the diced ingredients and lime juice.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Grits Dressing
steps: Preheat oven to 350F. Spray a 9x13 casserole dish with cooking spray.
In an oversized stock pot, use the water and grits to prepare the grits according to package instructions. You want the grits to be stiff when done cooking.
Saute the onion and celery in butter.

Add the sauteed vegetables, bread, and the remaining ingredients (stock, eggs, pimientos, sage, poultry seasoning, salt, and pepper) to the grits. Stir well. The mixture should be quite thick but not stiff - better too thick than too thin. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Spoon the dressing into a lightly greased 9x13 pan. Bake at 350F for about 30-45 minutes, or until set in the middle.
notes: A recipe from the mother's side of the family, traced back at least to Aunt Katie's great-grandmother from Alabama. Served every year at Thanksgiving and Christmas; a dish rarely encountered outside the family.
source: Aunt Katie (family recipe, traced to great-grandmother from Alabama)

title: Green Ass Green Chili
steps: Oil and salt the chicken, then roast at 450F for 15 minutes; cube when done. Alternatively: cube raw chicken, toss in corn starch, and brown in a Dutch oven, removing when partially cooked and setting aside for step 7.
Meanwhile, char the poblano on a direct flame (or combine with peppers in step 3 instead).
Broil the jalapeno and tomatillo until charred.
Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven. Add the onion to sweat.
While the onion cooks, clean and deseed the poblano, and chop the jalapeno and tomatillo. Add these and the green chili to a blender with chicken stock to cover, and blend into a bright green paste.
When the onion is soft, add the garlic.
Add the cubed chicken, cumin, and oregano, then mix.
Add the chili paste to the pot and stir for a few quick seconds.
Add about 2 cups of chicken stock, adjusting depending on the water content of the peppers, until desired consistency is reached.
Bring the mixture up to a strong simmer and add the potato and carrot.
Add smoked salt and reduce to a simmer until the potato and carrot are soft.
Taste for salt and pepper.
Serve with chopped cilantro, sour cream and/or pepper jack, and tortillas.

title: Fried Chicken

ingredients.name: buttermilk
ingredients.unit: to taste (enough to cover chicken for brining/dredging)

steps: If time allows, soak chicken pieces in buttermilk for at least 30 minutes (or up to overnight in the fridge) to tenderize and flavor.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs and a splash of buttermilk to make an egg wash.
In a separate bowl or dish, combine the flour with garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika, Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper.
Remove chicken from the buttermilk, letting excess drip off. Dredge in the seasoned flour, then dip in the egg wash, then dredge again in the seasoned flour for a thick coating.
Heat about 1-2 inches of oil in a heavy skillet or Dutch oven to 325-350F.
Fry the chicken in batches, without crowding the pan, for about 12-15 minutes per side (longer for bone-in pieces), until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165F.
Remove and drain on a wire rack or paper towels. Let rest a few minutes before serving.
notes: Generic fried chicken method - chicken quantity and exact seasoning amounts need to be measured and edited next time this is made.

title: Cream Gravy

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.unit: to taste (added 1/3 cup at a time)

steps: Melt the butter in a large pan.
Slowly sprinkle the flour into the butter.
Let cook for 2-3 minutes, creating a blonde roux.
Slowly add the milk, about 1/3 cup at a time, thoroughly mixing until clumps are gone and the desired consistency is reached.
Add salt to taste.
Add a healthy amount of black pepper.

title: Cornbread
steps: Preheat oven to 425F, placing a cast iron skillet into the oven to heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together the dry ingredients (cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt).
Whisk in the milk, buttermilk, butter, and eggs.
Carefully remove the skillet from the oven and reduce the oven temperature to 375F.
Coat the hot skillet with butter or bacon grease.
Pour the batter into the skillet and place on the center rack in the oven.
Bake for about 20-25 minutes, until the center is firm and a toothpick comes out clean.
Allow to cool for 10-15 minutes.

title: Sterling's Way Chili

ingredients.name: dried chiles (New Mexico/California, Guajillo, Pasilla, or a combination)
salt
ingredients.unit: to taste (plus 1 Tbsp for chile paste)

steps: Place the chiles in a straight-sided large skillet over medium-low heat and gently toast until fragrant, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Don't let them burn or they'll turn bitter. Place the chiles in a bowl, cover with very hot water, and soak until soft, 15 to 45 minutes, turning once or twice.

Drain the chiles; split them and remove stems and seeds (a brief rinse helps remove seeds, but don't wash away the flesh). Place the chiles in a blender and add the cumin, black pepper, 1 tablespoon salt, and 1/4 cup water. Puree, adding more water as needed and scraping down the sides occasionally, until a smooth, slightly fluid paste forms with only the tiniest bits of skin remaining. Set the chili paste aside.

Return the skillet to medium-high heat and melt 2 tablespoons of the lard. When it begins to smoke, swirl to coat and add half of the beef. Lightly brown on at least two sides, about 3 minutes per side, reducing heat if the meat threatens to burn. Transfer to a bowl and repeat with 2 more tablespoons of lard and the remaining beef. Reserve.

Let the skillet cool slightly, then place over medium-low heat. Melt the remaining 1 tablespoon of lard; add the onion and garlic and cook gently for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the stock and 2 cups water, gradually whisking in the masa harina to avoid lumps. Stir in the reserved chili paste, scraping the bottom of the skillet to loosen browned bits. Add the reserved beef and any juices, and bring to a simmer over high heat. Reduce heat to the barest possible simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the meat is tender but still somewhat firm and 1.5 to 2 cups of thickened but still liquid sauce surrounds the meat, about 2 hours.

Stir in the brown sugar and vinegar thoroughly, and add more salt to taste. Gently simmer 10 minutes more. It may look like there is excess sauce at this point. Turn off the heat and let the chili stand for at least 30 minutes, during which the meat will absorb about half of the remaining sauce. Stir in additional broth or water if the mixture seems too dry, or let it simmer longer if too loose and wet (partially crushing the beef cubes with the back of a spoon can help them absorb more sauce). Adjust salt, sugar, or vinegar to taste.
Reheat gently and serve in individual bowls with a dollop of sour cream on top and a lime wedge on the side.
notes: Given by brother-in-law Sterling. More of a braised meat in sauce than a traditional ground-meat chili.

title: Chili 2.0
steps: CHILI SLURRY: Bring a large pot of water to a boil - about as much as you would use to boil pasta.
Dice the onion (roughly medium-small).
Peel 6-10 cloves of garlic.
Clip the stems off the dried chiles and empty out and discard any loose seeds.
Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Toast the chiles for about 90-120 seconds - be careful not to burn them, or everything going forward will taste bitter.
Toss the chiles into the boiling water and lower the heat. Simmer for about 10 minutes.
When pulling the chiles from the water, save at least 2 cups of the water for later.
In the same pan used to toast the chiles, add 1/2-1 tablespoon of oil, butter, or tallow. Add the diced onion and caramelize until translucent with mostly browned edges.

Add the chiles, onions, and garlic to a blender along with the 16oz of beef stock. If too thick to blend, add some of the reserved chile water or more stock. Blend on high until completely smooth. Set aside.

BROWN THE MEAT: In a large Dutch oven (or a pan, if finishing in a crockpot), brown the meat, working in batches if needed. While browning, season with salt, pepper, chili powder, chili flakes, garlic powder, and onion powder. Brown well, then remove most of the grease, leaving the fond.

COOK: If cooking/finishing in the Dutch oven (best results), get all the meat into the hot Dutch oven and deglaze with a pour of Worcestershire sauce. If finishing in a crock pot, put the meat in there instead.
Add 6-10 cloves of minced garlic (or 2.5 tablespoons of garlic paste).
Immediately add the crushed tomatoes.
Add the chili slurry.
Add the remaining dry ingredients (beef bouillon, soy sauce, and any remaining seasoning to taste).
Simmer for at least 2 hours, ideally 4-6 hours.
notes: Latest iteration of a chili recipe tweaked often for competitions. Same chili slurry base doubles as a starting point for several variations: barbacoa tacos (brown a chuck roast, braise in the slurry until falling apart, shred, then griddle in tortillas with Oaxaca or mozzarella cheese); a more classic ballpark-style chili dog/burger topping (blend to a smoother consistency); a chili con queso base for queso or cheese enchiladas; and a New Mexico-style meat stew (swap the ground meat for cubed chuck roast or ribeye, skip the crushed tomatoes, braise, and serve with flour tortillas). Arbol chiles and cayenne are the main heat controls to adjust to taste.

title: Chicken Parmesan
steps: Preheat oven and add the cutlets (using frozen method).
Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Heat the tomato sauce in a pan on the stove. If making homemade sauce, start with the sauce first.
When the cutlets are about 3/4 of the way through their cook time, remove from the oven, add a dollop of tomato sauce, cover with mozzarella cheese, and place back in the oven.
Cook the pasta.

Assemble in a shallow bowl or plate: start with a bed of pasta, add a ladle of tomato sauce, place the chicken cutlet on top, and add an additional bit of sauce. Garnish with fresh basil ribbons and enjoy.
notes: Directions given are for the frozen-cutlet method.

title: Cheesy Potato Casserole
steps: Set out the hash browns to thaw, or if pressed for time, microwave in 10-second bursts - not to cook them, just to break apart the solid chunk.
Set aside 1/2 cup of cheese.
Mix the remaining ingredients together in a casserole dish.
Cover the top with the remaining cheese.
If eating now, bake at 375F for about 35-40 minutes, or until bubbly. Otherwise, wrap with foil and return to the fridge until ready to cook.
notes: Pretty forgiving dish - can be cooked alongside other holiday sides at temps anywhere from 350-400F if needed, just keep an eye on it.

title: Cheddar Crackers
steps: Preheat the oven to 375F.
Mix ingredients together in a bowl.
Scoop into mounds on a baking sheet.
Bake until melted and golden brown.
notes: Holiday crackers Aunt Katie brings over for Thanksgiving and Christmas.

title: Carnitas

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.unit: to taste (enough to help cover meat)

steps: Cut the pork into 2-inch cubes.
Add the pork to a large pot with the orange juice, water, beer, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 2 hours. Do not touch the meat.

After 2 hours, turn the heat up to medium-high and continue cooking until all the liquid has evaporated and the pork fat has rendered, about 45 minutes. Stir a few times to keep the pork from sticking to the bottom of the pot.
The pork is ready when browned. There will still be liquid fat in the pot - scoop the pork out with a slotted spoon onto a paper towel-covered plate to drain.
Shred and serve.

title: Cain's Sauce
steps: Mix all ingredients together in a bowl until fully combined.

title: Biscuits

ingredients.name: melted butter or heavy cream (for brushing tops)

steps: Preheat the oven to 450F.
Sift together the dry ingredients in a large mixing bowl.
Mix in 1 cup of cold buttermilk, just until the crumbs are thoroughly moistened. Add up to 1/4 cup additional buttermilk if needed. The dough should be slightly sticky but not overly wet.
Cube the butter or shortening and cut it into the dry ingredients using a pastry blender, or pulse in a food processor, until crumbly and resembling peas.

Roll or pat out on a lightly floured surface about 3/4-1 inch thick. Cut into rounds using a 2-inch cookie cutter dipped in flour. Do not twist the dough with the cutter - cut, then lift straight up. Re-roll any scraps and repeat.
Place biscuits 2 inches apart on the baking sheet. Brush the tops with melted butter or heavy cream.
Bake at 450F for 13-15 minutes, until lightly golden and puffed.
Brush with melted butter after removing from the oven. Serve immediately.

title: BBQ Sauce (TX Style)

ingredients.name: store bought starter or homemade base BBQ sauce

notes: Based on Dad's evolving recipe, taught while living in the Shepherd's Glen house. Amounts and method not yet written - to be filled in.

title: Baked Ziti

ingredients.name: tomato sauce (store bought starter or scratch)

steps: Boil water for the pasta; once ready, salt the water and cook the pasta.
Preheat oven to 375F.

If using pork sausage, brown it in a pan, mince the garlic and add it in toward the end to soften, then stir both into the tomato sauce. (If skipping sausage, saute the garlic briefly in a bit of oil before stirring into the sauce.)
Add a smear of tomato sauce to the baking pan (roughly 9x9 inches).
Drain the pasta and transfer it into the baking pan.
Add the rest of the tomato sauce.
Add a few heaping dollops of ricotta cheese.
Top and cover with mozzarella - if using shredded, sprinkle over the top; if using fresh, add large thick slices.
Place in the oven for about 30-45 minutes, or until the cheese starts to do what cheese do.
Garnish with a couple leaves of shredded basil.
notes: An attempt to reverse-engineer a baked ziti from a place near the Taurus house, enjoyed with Paige from 2015-19. Not based on any known original recipe.

title: Cajun Garlic Cream Sauce Shrimp over Rice

ingredients.name: white rice, uncooked (sushi rice or any white rice works)
lemon (juice of the heel, not a full half)
Pecorino Romano rind, chopped into small pieces (melted into sauce)

steps: Cook the rice separately (rice cooker works great) according to normal method.
Season the shrimp generously with cajun seasoning.
Cook the shrimp in a 10-inch pan until done, then move to a bowl and set aside, leaving the fond in the pan.
In the same pan, add the shallot and cook for about 1 minute.
Add the butter and begin to deglaze the pan with the butter/shallot mixture.
Juice the heel of the lemon into the pan (not the full half).
Add the garlic and cook for another 45 seconds to 1 minute - do not let it burn.
Add the heavy cream along with the pecorino pieces and mascarpone. Continue to stir until the sauce is smooth and creamy.
Add the shrimp back in and stir/cook for another minute or two, then turn off the heat.
To serve: spoon a scoop and a half of rice into a shallow bowl, then spoon a healthy scoop and a half of the shrimp and cream sauce over the top. Finish with grated pecorino.
notes: Freestyled dish, written down for the first time - served gumbo-style, thick cream sauce spooned over separately-cooked rice (dirty rice style plating). Can stand alone but goes well with roasted broccolini, broccoli, asparagus, or another green veg on the side.

title: Salmon Croquettes

ingredients.name: yellow onion, grated on coarse cheese grater

steps: Bake: Place salmon in a baking dish and bake at 450F for 14-18 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 135-145F.
Add: Grate the yellow onion using the coarse setting of a cheese grater. Add the grated onion, panko, bell pepper, garlic, egg, chives, parsley, salt, and pepper to a medium bowl.
Mix: When the salmon is done, transfer to a plate and use two forks to shred it. After it cools for a few minutes, add it to the bowl with the other ingredients. Mix until well combined.
Form: Use a 1/4 cup measure to portion out 1/4 cup-sized balls, placing them on a large plate.
Finish forming: Lightly press the balls down into thick patties. Make sure the ingredients are tightly packed/squeezed together so the patties do not fall apart.
Heat: Add about 1/2 inch of oil to a large pan. Turn heat to medium-high and wait until the oil reaches 325-350F.
Fry: Very carefully slide the croquettes into the pan, making sure they do not break apart. Add as many as possible without overcrowding. Cook for 1-2 minutes per side, until deep golden.
Season: Use a slotted spatula to remove the croquettes from the oil onto a paper towel-lined plate. Sprinkle generously with salt.
Repeat until all croquettes are fried. Serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Amounts not yet measured - this is made by eye/feel. To be measured and locked in next time it is made.

title: Tartar Sauce
steps: Stir together the mayonnaise, relish, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, capers, dill or parsley, and onion or shallot in a medium bowl.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Chill, covered, for at least 30 minutes before serving to let the flavors meld. Keeps in the fridge for about a week.
notes: Generic homemade tartar sauce, put together to go with Salmon Croquettes. Adjust relish/lemon/dill to taste.

title: French Onion Soup

ingredients.name: large yellow onions (about 3 lb), peeled and thinly sliced
shallot, peeled and thinly sliced (prepped with the onions)
kosher salt, plus more to taste
black pepper, plus more to taste

steps: Melt the butter in a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onions and shallot along with 1/2 teaspoon salt, stir, and cover, letting them soften for 5 minutes. Remove the lid and let the onions caramelize until golden brown over medium heat, stirring occasionally. Adjust heat if browning too quickly - caramelization may take 45 to 60 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the broth in a saucepan over low heat.
Once the onions are caramelized, add the sherry vinegar to the pot and allow the mixture to come to a boil. Stir in the flour and let it thicken for a minute or two.
Slowly add the warm broth, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and the pepper to the onion mixture. Boil uncovered for 10 minutes. Add more salt and pepper to taste.
Heat the broiler and arrange individual ovenproof casseroles on a baking sheet. Ladle soup into the casseroles and cover the top with bread slices. Sprinkle each casserole generously with Gruyere.
Broil for a minute or two, watching carefully, until the cheese melts and browns. Serve immediately.
notes: Can prepare through step 4 up to 2 months in advance - thaw, reheat, then top with bread and cheese and broil to serve. Sherry vinegar used in place of wine.
